title: The Sahara Desert
text: The Sahara is the world's largest hot desert and the third-largest desert overall, after Antarctica and the Arctic. Covering approximately 9.2 million square kilometers, it occupies much of North Africa, stretching from the Atlantic Ocean to the Red Sea. The desert is characterized by extreme temperature variation, with daytime temperatures regularly exceeding 40°C while nighttime temperatures can fall below freezing. Despite its harsh conditions, the Sahara is home to diverse life including camels, fennec foxes, and various reptiles adapted to arid environments. About 25% of the Sahara is sand dunes (ergs), with the remainder covered by rocky plateaus (hamada), gravel plains (reg), and occasional oases.
